newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money falls on rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money falls on rate cut.

text.p: A 0.25 percentage-point cut in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate pulled down Manila overnight money to an average of 10.03125 percent on Friday from 10.28125 percent, traders said.
"The market was expecting it (the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate) to go down but not this soon," a dealer said.
Done rates were at a lower range from 10.0625 to ten percent.
The market had 22 lenders and 12 borrowers, as market volume fell to 7.539 billion from 9.965 billion pesos.
Traders said the Central Bank's action prodded banks to buy more of its special series T-bills and other bills.
"They're looking at a further drop in interest rates," a foreign bank dealer said.
Seven banks polled by Reuters gave bid rates of 10.01 to 10.05 for three-month bills.
